assertions.name: q_beta_reference_is_truncated_to_eight_figures
assertions.source: codata_constants.Q_BETA_MEV = 0.7823334099999999999999999999999999999999999999999994098296040398407753 differs from the witness's own reference by 8.8209e-10 — a truncated reference in a corpus that computes at 60 dps. Recorded, not fixed.

description: The corpus establishes (qou-e58e, 11 nuclei, five q) that bar: q -> 1/q IS proton<->neutron conjugation, and at bond level p<->n is exactly z<->zbar. Q_beta's element Delta = B_n - B_p is a p<->n DIFFERENCE, so under that conjugation it should be bar-ODD: bar(tr_M(Delta)) = -tr_M(Delta). Tested on the two candidate elements the fork leaves open. Delta_S (normal-form difference, tr_M AFFINE in z): bar-odd iff bar(z) = z - h, ONE branch, satisfied by EXACTLY the two admissible functionals (z=q augmentation, z_D = q^3/(q^2+1)) and by neither z=1 (published) nor z_C (excised C). Delta_L (eleven-crossing word difference, tr_M QUADRATIC in z): two branches, satisfied by NONE of the four, the admissible pair included. So under the isospin reading Delta_S + admissible functional is bar-odd and Delta_L + admissible functional is not. AND THE WHOLE SPAN, which is the statement that matters: the admissible TRACES are 2-dimensional and the two Markov points span them, so testing only those points under-claims. Measured, on Delta_S BOTH basis traces have vanishing bar-odd defect => EVERY admissible trace is bar-odd; on Delta_L neither does and the two defects are NOT proportional over Q (ratio (q^2+1)^2/(q^4+1) is q-dependent) => a*dA + b*dB = 0 forces a = b = 0, so ONLY THE ZERO TRACE is bar-odd. That is a genuine exclusion of Delta_L WITHIN the admissible span over Q, not a sampling argument. NOT established: coefficients in Q(q) (bar acts on them too; scaling by f(q) rescales Q_beta, a different physical claim) and non-admissible z (Delta_L's second branch is involution-consistent, so some inadmissible z may work). Reached with NO anchor and NO experimental input. Nothing wired, no functional adopted, no element declared canonical.

Delta_L.verdict: ONLY the zero trace is bar-odd

scope.tier: exclusion within the admissible span over Q; scope-(a) outside it
scope.established: Delta_S is bar-odd under EXACTLY the two admissible functionals and, more strongly, on the WHOLE admissible trace span; Delta_L is bar-odd under none of the four and, on the span with constant coefficients, ONLY at the zero trace (the two bar-odd defects are non-proportional over Q). A genuine exclusion within the span.
scope.NOT_established: (i) coefficients in Q(q) — bar acts on them too, and scaling a trace by f(q) rescales Q_beta, so it is a different physical claim, untested either way; (ii) that Delta_L can never be bar-odd for ANY z — its second branch is involution-consistent, so some INADMISSIBLE z may work, which is irrelevant to the physics but means the universal claim was not shown
scope.premise: bar is p<->n conjugation, measured in qou-e58e over 11 nuclei; a p<->n DIFFERENCE should therefore be bar-odd. If that reading is wrong, the criterion loses its motivation and this becomes an observation about two rational functions.
